page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What polymeric means, and the unit
lines: In orthoboric acid H₃BO₃ the boron atom
is sp² hybridised and bonded to three OH
groups, so one molecule is a flat BO₃
triangle. Each of its three OH groups can
steps.why: The shape of the single molecule is what makes the extended structure possible: a flat triangle with an OH group at each corner can pack beside its neighbours in the same plane.
common_mistakes: Calling the boron sp³. Boron here has three bonded groups and no lone pair, so it is sp² and the unit is planar.
Writing H₃BO₃ with four oxygen atoms. It has three; four oxygens belong to the ion [B(OH)₄]⁻.
steps.memory_tip: Three OH groups on a flat triangle means three places to hydrogen bond.
steps.margin_note: Say what polymeric means first, then the flat sp² unit, then the linking.

steps.label: Hydrogen bonding into layers

lines.text: Repeating hydrogen bonds link BO₃ units

lines: The OH group of one H₃BO₃ molecule forms
a hydrogen bond to an oxygen of the next.
This joins many BO₃ units into a two
This repeating hydrogen bonded network is
why boric acid is described as polymeric.
steps.why: The link between one unit and the next is a hydrogen bond, not a covalent bond, and that same link repeats right across the layer. It is the repetition that makes the structure extended instead of a set of separate molecules.
common_mistakes: Saying the units are joined by covalent bonds. The link between one unit and the next is a hydrogen bond.
Describing a three dimensional network. The hydrogen bonded units form flat layers, and the layers are held to each other by much weaker van der Waals forces.
steps.memory_tip: The same hydrogen bond repeats across a flat sheet, so the structure is polymeric.
steps.margin_note: The words hydrogen bond and layer carry this half of the answer.

insider_note: The question is about the link between molecules, so the hydrogen bonding must be stated in words and not left to a drawing.
